distinguishing_features: Applies a 2-5 mm compliant polyurethane elastomer layer directly to the impeller impact surface.
Uses elastic energy absorption and extended particle-contact duration to reduce transmitted peak stress.
Physically prevents erosion rather than predicting remaining life from motor-current signatures.
Implements the change by surface preparation, primer application, dip-coating, curing, and installation.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce erosion of a rotating slurry-pump impeller caused by high-velocity quartz-particle impacts without changing the impeller geometry or operating duty and while preserving hydraulic performance.
parsed.viable_reason: The asserted contact-time and force reduction is physically unsupported, a 1 ms contact at 20 m/s would require millimetric-to-centimetric deformation inconsistent with a 2-5 mm coating, and pressure drop alone is not a valid erosion or coating-integrity test.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The closest art discloses predictive monitoring and conventional hardening, not the proposed impact-damping mechanism in which a compliant surface layer lowers quartz-induced contact stress.
